articles.title: ‘Pyre’ Gets 200 Shows After Vinod Kapri Claims 75% of Shows Were Cut After ‘Ramayana’ Release
articles.description: After filmmaker Vinod Kapri claimed that Pyre lost nearly 75 per cent of its theatrical shows following the release of Ramayana, the independent film has secured over 200 additional shows from November 13. According to Vinod, Pyre had initially secured around 400 screens, with positive word of mouth helping it attract audiences. However, he alleged that the number of screens fell to fewer than 100 after Ramayana arrived in theatres. He also claimed that several theatre owners pulled the film despite it running to houseful shows. Following his allegations, the All India Cine Workers Association (AICWA) appealed to Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw to intervene in the matter. Now, the National Award-winning filmmaker has thanked audiences for supporting his independent film and helping it return to more screens. ‘Pyre’ Gets 200 Screens In a post on X, formerly Twitter, Kapri announced that Pyre would receive more than 200 additional shows from Friday, November 13. He wrote, “Pyre is getting its shows back! Over 200 shows of Pyre are being added from Friday, 13th November. A heartfelt thank you to our audiences for standing by this little independent film and making this possible.” Kapri also expressed gratitude to the cinema chains that supported the film and helped take the story of Amma and Bubu to a wider audience. He added, “Your love, trust and support have brought us back to more screens. A big thank you to Cinépolis India and PVR Cinemas for supporting PYRE and giving more audiences an opportunity to experience Amma and Bubu’s story. This journey belongs to all of you.” ‘Pyre’ Enters Oscars Race Pyre has entered the Oscars race through the independent submission route. Meanwhile, Gondhal remains India’s official entry for the Academy Awards. Another Indian film, Angh, directed by Theja Rio, has also become eligible for consideration after winning the Platform Award at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival. Nitesh Tiwari’s Ramayana has also entered the Oscars race through the same independent submission route. Speaking about the decision to pursue the Academy Awards, Vinod told India Today, “We believe independent cinema deserves the opportunity to compete on its own merits. Our decision to pursue the Academy Awards through the applicable independent submission route is an extension of that belief. This is not just a journey for our film; it is also a journey for the many independent filmmakers who continue to tell stories against all odds.” About ‘Pyre’ Pyre follows an elderly couple who have spent decades waiting for their only son to return home. He continues to write letters to his parents, assuring them that he will come back. Meanwhile, villagers begin leaving their homes one by one after their children invite them to places where they have found better livelihoods. One particularly poignant scene in the trailer shows Bubu preparing a funeral pyre for his wife. He says that if she dies, he will not be able to carry her downhill for her final rites. Shot in Uttarakhand, the film has won 18 international awards, including 15 Best Film honours at festivals and events in Washington, DC, Chicago, Canada, Spain, Boston, Stuttgart, London and Birmingham. The film features two first-time performers in its lead roles. Padam Singh Kapri, 80, and Heera Devi, 70, are residents of Uttarakhand who had never faced a camera before the project. Padam Singh, a retired Army serviceman, plays a character who shares his name, while Heera Devi portrays Tulsi. Pyre was released in Indian theatres in Hindi on October 30 and is scheduled to arrive in Malayalam on December 11.

articles.title: Kedarnath Dham Closing 2026: Temple Doors Shut For Six Months, Know When The Shrine Will Reopen In 2027
articles.description: Kedarnath Dham Closing 2026: The doors of the world-famous eleventh Jyotirlinga, Shri Kedarnath Dham, located in Uttarakhand, have been closed for the winter season today, November 11, 2026, on the auspicious occasion of Bhai Dooj. At exactly 8:30 am, amid traditional Vedic chanting, rituals, and the sound of local musical instruments, the main gate of the temple was closed for the next six months. Despite the severe cold, thousands of Shiva devotees were present at the Dham to witness this historic and emotional moment. Panchmukhi Doli Leaves For Ukhimath Accompanied By The Tunes Of The Army Band After the closing of the doors was completed, the Panchmukhi Utsav Doli, the movable idol of Lord Kedarnath, was brought out of the temple's sanctum sanctorum. Amid the devotional tunes of the Indian Army band and chants of "Har Har Mahadev," the palanquin departed for its winter residence, the Shri Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath. For the next six months, devotees will be able to visit and worship Baba Kedarnath only at the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath. The ancient Omkareshwar Temple, located at an altitude of approximately 1,311 meters above sea level in Ukhimath, Rudraprayag district, Uttarakhand, is the winter seat of Lord Kedarnath and Madhyamaheshwar. During the six months of winter, the five-headed festival palanquin of Baba Kedarnath resides here, where devotees perform ritualistic worship. The Journey Of The Year 2026 Created A New Record This year's Chardham Yatra witnessed unprecedented enthusiasm among devotees. According to temple committee data, more than 19.14 lakh devotees paid obeisance at the shrine of Baba Kedarnath during the 2026 pilgrimage season. Despite adverse weather and difficult routes, the devotees' faith remained unshaken, making this year's pilgrimage a resounding success. When Will The Doors Of Kedarnath Dham Open In 2027? For devotees planning to visit Baba Kedarnath next year, information on the tentative opening dates has been revealed. According to tradition, the doors of Gangotri and Yamunotri shrines open on Akshaya Tritiya, followed by Kedarnath a few days later. Possible date: Akshaya Tritiya falls on May 9 in 2027. Therefore, there is a strong possibility that the doors of Kedarnath Temple will open between May 9 and May 12, 2027 (especially around May 11). Official announcement: The exact auspicious time for the opening of the doors is determined annually on Mahashivratri. This year, Mahashivratri falls on March 6, 2027. The official date will be announced on this day after the religious leaders at the Omkareshwar Temple in Ukhimath have calculated the calendar. Important Rules Related To Travel And Helicopter Booking Devotees wishing to travel next year will be required to register online on the official Uttarakhand Tourism Department portal in March or April 2027. Furthermore, booking tickets for the helicopter service will be done only through the official IRCTC HeliYatra website. For any latest and accurate information related to the Yatra, devotees can keep an eye on the official website of Badrinath-Kedarnath Temple Committee (BKTC). Consult a relevant expert before acting on any information or information.
